messages:
Uma Patel: Quick check — the route YAML preview shows "Valid" (green) but when I hit Save I get 'YAML parse error: line 12: mapping values are not allowed'. No helpful cursor or highlight. Anyone else?

Matt B: I saw this with trailing tabs in map values. Can you paste the YAML? Maybe the preview lints only schema, not parse-level whitespace?

Uma Patel: Pasting minimal repro:
```yaml
routes:
  - id: test-route
    match:
      path: /foo
    upstream:
      host: example
    metadata:
      team: infra  
```
I had two trailing spaces after 'infra' — preview still green.

Li Chen: Hmm — console preview runs jsonschema validation after converting parsed YAML to canonical form; but we only surface schema issues, not parse errors. Save goes through a stricter parse step (js-yaml with strict mode) which fails on invalid tabs/spaces. We should show parse failures inline.

Uma Patel: Can we change preview to run a lightweight parse check first and show inline hint under the editor? Even a subtle warning icon would help.

Matt B: Agreed. Also for quicker repro, console-bot: note a telemetry flag maybe? @console-bot can we log parse_errors v=1 for this route-editor save? :eyes: 

console-bot: Logged event route_editor.parse_error with sample_hash=0x3f9a, user=uma at 1719246810

Li Chen: Implementation note: js-yaml throws with line/col. We can add pre-parse step and map the error -> editor marker. Should be ~2 dev days.

Uma Patel: Sounds good. Can we also show a one-line tooltip explaining difference between schema vs parse errors? Example text: "Parse errors prevent saving. Schema warnings are advisory." Small UX change.

Matt B: +1. I'll open a tiny RFC in a PR and add a unit test that injects trailing tabs. Assign to @Li for the editor patch.

Li Chen: Will do. Thanks.
